Redesign the Q1 attainability census so it actually measures state-carrying items at depth. Under the frozen item-blind FIFO BFS (budget=250, depth=6) only 72 of 556 discovered hop>=3 pages (12.95%) were ever fetched, so `deep_with_controls` conflates 'no named input/select at depth' with 'deep page never fetched'. mdBook/doc.rust-lang.org (220 deep) and Sphinx/pandas.pydata.org (9 deep) fetched ZERO deep pages. The census must (a) fetch/observe a defined sample of DEEP pages, or (b) report two separate quantities: DEEP pages discovered vs DEEP pages fetched with controls observed, and must not emit `engines_with_zero_deep` as if deep state-carrying absence were measured when it was not.

validity_findings.finding: Independent reproduction confirms the frozen outcome-bearing code is fatally defective, so the Q2/Q3 measurement transaction genuinely could not complete. Running the frozen execute_module.py `--stage discovery` offline against the producer's own raw/channel_docs.jsonl and raw/structural.jsonl exits 1 with `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'int'` at execute_module.py:995 (host_census) and would also fail at :1000. Cause: bfs_structural deliberately writes controls_seen=None for discovered-but-unfetched pages (execute_module.py:443-444), but the discovery loop assumes an int. The crash occurs on the first pool host (doc.rust-lang.org, 220 unfetched hop-3 pages) before evaluate_items or compute_metrics run, so no items.jsonl exists. The producer's status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID / outcome=NOT_APPLICABLE mapping is therefore correct per EXPERIMENT_PACKET.md section 1 (code/substrate failure must not be encoded as scientific falsification).

validity_findings.finding: The Q1 'state-carrying DEEP item' census that the producer presents as partial evidence is confounded by the frozen crawl policy and does not measure what the mandate's Q1 asks. Recomputed from raw/structural.jsonl: 556 hop>=3 pages were discovered across the pool, but only 72 (12.95%) were ever fetched, so their state-carrying status is unobserved. Per host: doc.rust-lang.org 0/220 fetched, pandas.pydata.org 0/9, docs.pytest.org 4/160, quotes.toscrape.com 10/99, jekyllrb.com 23/24, react.dev 7/8, docs.readthedocs.io 28/36. `engines_with_zero_deep`=14 therefore mixes engines where deep pages were fetched and genuinely had no named input/select (Jekyll, custom, Docusaurus among fetched subsets) with engines where deep pages were never fetched at all (mdBook=220, Sphinx/pandas=9). The mandate's Q1 is not answered for the unmeasured engines; the census measures crawl observability, not the prevalence of deep state-carrying content.

A producer observation is factually wrong. result.json#observations[4] and report.md sections 2.2/2.3 assert that the zero-DEEP engines' deep pages were 'all ... unfetched (controls_seen=null) due to BFS budget exhaustion', and the report table marks jekyllrb.com and quotes.toscrape.com as 'All unfetched (budget)'. Recomputation from raw/structural.jsonl shows jekyllrb.com fetched 23 of 24 deep pages (all controls_seen=0), react.dev/Docusaurus fetched 7 of 8 (all 0), and quotes.toscrape.com fetched 10 of 99 (all 0). Those zeros are measured absences of the named_controls unit, not budget artifacts. The budget artifact is real only for doc.rust-lang.org (mdBook 220 unfetched) and pandas.pydata.org (Sphinx 9 unfetched) on the deep frontier. This misattributes genuine observations to non-observation and inflates the claimed budget confound in one direction while understating the genuine zero.

result.json.metrics.per_engine was not produced by the frozen outcome-bearing code (which crashed before compute_metrics at execute_module.py:685 ran) and is internally inconsistent. Sphinx-RTD reports n_deep=32 but hop_distribution={'3':94,'4':101,'5':1} summing to 196; the frozen compute_metrics builds hop_distribution only from the live admitted items (execute_module.py:729), so 32 is the only value consistent with its own rule. Five engines with deep_total>0 (Docusaurus 8, Jekyll 24, Sphinx 9, custom 99, mdBook 220) report empty hop_distribution. pool_engines_census duplicates a deep_with_controls count (Sphinx-RTD=32) under an ambiguous name. No derived artifact or script documents the external computation. The host-level host_census is reproducible (audit matched all 20 host rows exactly from raw), but the engine-level block is not trustworthy as written.

The design-contract-v2 gate treatment_liveness passed without certifying that the measured object is executable. design_review.json and spec.json.freeze_eligibility.treatment_liveness assert the complete pipeline 'was executed end-to-end offline ... without errors', but the actual frozen discovery entry point fails immediately on the real structural graph (AUDIT-VF-01). The offline fixture (run_controls) exercises bfs_structural and evaluate_items directly and never constructs a structural row containing discovered-but-unfetched pages, so the fatal path was untested. This is the same failure class the Director flagged for the superseded EXP-FRONTIER-38085197666 (checks declared PASS while the underlying object was not runnable); freeze_eligibility as implemented did not prevent it.

Packet-state labeling is defensible but not defined by the frozen rule. The frozen decision_rule G1 maps only V1/V2/V3 failures to MEASUREMENT_INVALID; it does not specify the disposition for a runtime defect in the outcome code. The producer's MEASUREMENT_INVALID/NOT_APPLICABLE mapping is reasonable under EXPERIMENT_PACKET.md section 1, though BLOCKED is an equally defensible packet state (the outcome stage never executed end to end). Recorded for traceability; no scientific consequence.

claim_ceiling: MEASUREMENT_INVALID. No scientific claim about site-native discovery reachability (the mandate's Q2/Q3 and the H1/F1 tests) is supportable from this transaction; C-CROSSSITE retains its Codex effective status HYPOTHESIS and must not be updated by this packet. Independently confirmed and admissible: (a) a design/process-defect receipt - the frozen outcome-bearing module (CODE_SHA256 75a01d490ec81609cbf87a606f8cfa9227d07f07765b2eb4fd876fef2c8ff53a, verified equal to prereg.md section 16) crashes with a TypeError in its discovery entry point at execute_module.py:995/1000, so the Q2/Q3 measurement could not be taken and this is not a SUPPORTS, FALSIFIES or INCONCLUSIVE scientific result; (b) a bounded, externally derived and independent-reproduced Q1 observability census over the frozen 20-host pool - 556 hop>=3 pages discovered, 72 (12.95%) fetched, 32 carrying >=1 named input/select, all 32 on the single engine Sphinx-RTD (docs.readthedocs.io 28, docs.pytest.org 4). That census measures crawl observability under the frozen item-blind BFS budget=250, NOT the prevalence of deep state-carrying content: mdBook (220 deep) and Sphinx/pandas.pydata.org (9 deep) fetched zero deep pages, and the producer's claim that all zero-DEEP engines' deep pages were unfetched is false for jekyllrb.com, react.dev and quotes.toscrape.com. Do not read engines_with_zero_deep=14 as a Web fact; do not read per_engine.hop_distribution as valid; do not promote the discovery shortcut and do not close the discovery axis on this packet. The Director's recorded runner-up (persistence-maintenance/invalidation economics) remains an allocation decision, not a result of this experiment.
